title: At the lowest level space is a network of nodes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: At the lowest level space is a network of nodes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: At the lowest level, space is most likely a giant network of nodes defined only by their connections (and it suffices to consider nodes with exactly three connections), with ordinary space emerging as a large-scale limit.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And with this in mind I believe that what is by far the most likely is that at the lowest level space is in effect a giant network of nodes.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Space as a Network” (from p. 475), p. 475. Scope: fundamental structure of physical space

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-14: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.36

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing observations can constrain particular network models but cannot identify the claimed microscopic ontology. Resolution needs a specified dynamics and data sensitive to its distinctive small-scale effects.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Derive distinctive low-energy or propagation signatures from a trivalent network model and compare them with precision particle, gravitational, and astrophysical observations. Network-specific deviations would support it; observations incompatible with every such network realization would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Microscopic network structure is not directly observed.

The network dynamics are not specified.

Many continuum and discrete models share low-energy predictions.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.15
analysis feasibility: 0.25
discriminating power: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A network with only connectivity, including the trivalent case, is a definite hypothesis and could in principle be distinguished by a small-scale signature. Existing particle and cosmological constraints, and published network evolutions, do not isolate that signature from other discrete substrates. The data that would decide it are absent.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Derive a signature that is produced by a trivalent network substrate and not by other discrete spaces, then compare it with short-distance or cosmological measurements. A unique matched signature would support the claim; a theorem that every rival substrate produces the same signature would leave it unresolved.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Trivalence is stated as sufficient, so a different node degree would not by itself refute the network claim.

Causal sets, spin networks, and lattices can match the same large-scale three-dimensional observations.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.2
operationalizability: 0.4
data existence: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.22
discriminating power: 0.26
